sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Immediate Trigger**: The failure of the **Cripps Mission (1942)**, which offered only 'Dominion Status' and post-dated cheques, convinced Gandhi that British presence was the cause of communalism and failure to defend against Japan.
• **Ideological Shift**: Gandhi moved from 'non-violence as a creed' to 'non-violence as a policy', allowing for a more militant, spontaneous mass struggle.
• **Leadership Vacuum**: The **'Operation Zero Hour'** led to the arrest of all top-tier Congress leaders on August 9, 1942, resulting in a 'leaderless' movement driven by the masses.
• **Key Metric**: The movement saw the emergence of 'Parallel Governments' in regions like Ballia, Tamluk, and Satara, marking a shift from protest to governance.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Strikes, student protests, and picketing in Bombay, Delhi, and Calcutta.
Spontaneous reaction to the arrest of national leadership.
Prelims: Focus on the role of students and women.
Sabotage of communication lines, parallel governments in Satara, Midnapore, Ballia.
Shift to 'Do or Die' tactics; use of underground radio (Usha Mehta).
Mains: Decentralized nature of the movement.

items.definition: The British government's preemptive strike to arrest all top Congress leaders (Gandhi, Nehru, Patel) on the morning of August 9, 1942, to decapitate the movement.
Local administrative bodies established by rebels in areas where British authority collapsed, such as 'Jatiya Sarkar' in Tamluk (Midnapore).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Underground Network**: Led by Jayaprakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali to maintain momentum.
• **Congress Radio**: Operated by Usha Mehta from secret locations in Bombay to disseminate news.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Brutal state repression (Lathi charges, firing), lack of support from Muslim League, CPI, and Hindu Mahasabha.
• **Solutions**: The movement forced the British to realize that India could no longer be governed without the consent of its people, leading to the Wavell Plan.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-T-S' (Parallel Governments: Ballia, Tamluk, Satara).
• **Decoded Meaning**: B (Ballia - Chittu Pandey), T (Tamluk - Jatiya Sarkar), S (Satara - Prati Sarkar).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often states that the Communist Party of India (CPI) or the Muslim League supported the Quit India Movement. Both remained neutral or opposed it.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Spontaneous Mass Uprising' rather than 'Organized Movement' to describe the 1942 struggle.

keyTakeaways: The movement was leaderless due to Operation Zero Hour, making it a truly grassroots struggle.
It marked the end of the British 'moral' claim to rule India.
The emergence of parallel governments demonstrated the readiness of Indians for self-governance.
